definitions.explanation: A verb that does not take a direct object. In Japanese grammar, intransitive verbs describe actions or states that happen on their own without an agent acting on something.

examples.japanese: 「{開|あ}く」は{自動詞|じどうし}です。
{自動詞|じどうし}は「を」を{取|と}らない。
examples.english: Intransitive verbs do not take the particle wo.

examples.japanese: {日本語|にほんご}では{自動詞|じどうし}と{他動詞|たどうし}の{区別|くべつ}が{大切|たいせつ}です。
examples.english: In Japanese, the distinction between intransitive and transitive verbs is important.

notes:
A grammatical term used in Japanese language study. Intransitive verbs ({自動詞|じどうし}) describe actions or changes that occur without a direct object, in contrast to transitive verbs ({他動詞|たどうし}).

COMMON PAIRS (intransitive / transitive):
・{開|あ}く / {開|あ}ける (open)
・{閉|し}まる / {閉|し}める (close)
・{始|はじ}まる / {始|はじ}める (begin)
・{壊|こわ}れる / {壊|こわ}す (break)

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
・Intransitive: {ドア|どあ}が{開|あ}く (the door opens — subject marked with が)
・Transitive: ドアを{開|あ}ける (open the door — object marked with を)
